content: Benchmark context k21 vs k31: Kmerind (TCBB 2017) distinct valid k-mers FALL with larger k (1909M@k21 vs 1670M@k31, 2052M@k15). Merfin (Nature Methods 2022 supp) k31=1.5x memory (123->183GB) + 1.6-2.6x compute vs k21; 72-89% distinct k-mers are singletons from errors. KMC paper Table2: Jellyfish RAM grows k22->k31 (50->87GB) runtime ~flat; KMC ~constant 32GB. ntStat 2025: Jellyfish 118GB@k25 vs KMC3 11.9GB+151GB disk. Small k=more distinct keys+more error singletons=bigger DRAM-bound table. No single head-to-head human k21-vs-k31 both-tool benchmark; profiling needed.
